deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Move from unprompted appreciation through the visible reframing process, the psychology-informed channel gap, a working market-gap need-state, one separate illustrative Maya use case, one explicit design brief, the solution proposition, a mechanism-level response to the gap and one shared live demo.
deck.evidence_rule: The displayed participant ratings and percentages—including the 72% and 78% Maya-slide placeholders—are disclosed in the slide footers as temporary rehearsal data because Ethan explicitly requested presentable test values; they must be replaced before the judged pitch. Published studies support only the adjacent channel mechanisms, not the practice values, plotted positions, Goldilocks gap, market sizing, demand or product superiority.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: A starting expression hypothesis visibly changes into an ordinary-day social-script question, then resolves through a Goldilocks channel gap into one authored object moving from maker to receiver.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the project territory, meet the product identity and team, then move immediately.

visual.composition: Use `Rethinking when we show appreciation.` as the project title above Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark on white. Keep the approved team name, team number and confirmed member names as one compact line once supplied.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Say the project title, name the team and move.
Blocked until team number and member-name spelling are confirmed.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time you showed someone appreciation or gratitude?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recall the last time they initiated an unprompted act of appreciation before the team names the problem.

visual.composition: One full-frame question ending with `appreciation or gratitude?` Do not put the birthday or event clarification on the slide. Do not mention letters, because that reveals a solution format before the problem is established. No counterpoint, supporting sentence or raise-hands prompt.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Ask the visible sender-framed appreciation-or-gratitude question and pause briefly. Then say aloud that birthdays, celebrations and major events do not count.
Do not mention letters, ask for raised hands or add the removed `we have never had more ways to talk` counterpoint.
A pause or difficulty remembering opens the story; it is not evidence.
Cultural transmission and fear of social judgment remain mechanisms to research, not facts to state.

motion.description: One question appears once; no staged subtext.

slides.claim: The unwritten rule: appreciation needs an occasion.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the team's process move from an expression hypothesis to a working contrast between socially prompted events and an unprompted ordinary day.

visual.composition: Stage five beats on one slide. Start with the team's hypothesis—`We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.` Then highlight only `show it.` Reveal the headline `The unwritten rule: appreciation needs an occasion.` with an event side: `celebration / milestone`, then `expected`, `socially understood` and `a clear prompt`. Next reveal the ordinary-day side: `no obvious prompt`, then `awkward`, `too much` and `intense`. Finish with the unchanged How Might We: `How might we make ordinary-day appreciation easier to send?` Preserve the paper-and-ink system and state in the footer that the cited papers are related mechanisms while the occasion framing remains a working hypothesis.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Start: `We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.` Highlight `show it`, then say: `That changed our framing. The unwritten rule is that appreciation needs an occasion.`

On the event side, say: `At a celebration or milestone, appreciation is expected, socially understood and has a clear prompt.` On the ordinary-day side, say: `On an ordinary day there is no obvious prompt, so it can feel awkward, too much or intense.`
Finish with the unchanged question: `How might we make ordinary-day appreciation easier to send?`

Treat the starting statement and occasion framing as working hypotheses, not prevalence findings. Kumar and Epley studied gratitude letters; Givi and Galak studied anticipated reactions to non-occasion gifts. These are related mechanisms, not proof that the proposed occasion rule is prevalent.

motion.description: Start on the hypothesis; build 1 highlights `show it`; build 2 reveals the unwritten-rule headline and event side; build 3 reveals the ordinary-day side and evidence boundary; build 4 lands the unchanged How Might We.

slides.claim: Psychology gave us three mechanisms to test.
slides.audience_takeaway: See three psychology-informed mechanisms across broad form families, then the Goldilocks combination the team is testing as a design target.

visual.composition: An impact-versus-friction map where each clearly visible circle behind a channel icon encodes how frequently that form family is received. Hand-drawn channel icons distinguish quick text, voice note / video call and handwritten letter / physical gift. Each reveal keeps one active full-navy form with one large, bounded psychological mechanism and author-year citation while previous forms recede: tone can be misread; voice can feel closer; thoughtfulness matters more than price. Keep numeric ratings on the survey-results slide. Finish on an unboxed `goldilocks zone`, marked by Cecelia's firefly mascot in the same deep navy as the deck typography, as a design target for high impact, low friction and repeatability. The high-contrast axes and footer keep the three encodings and evidence boundary explicit.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.

Say: `Psychology gave us three mechanisms to test: text can lose tone, voice can feel more connecting, and thoughtfulness—not price—is what helps care land. So the Goldilocks zone is our design target—not a discovered finding—for expression that is easy, legible and worth keeping.`
Do not explain paper methods unless asked in Q&A; the visible author-year citations establish the trail.
The papers support only the mechanism labels, not the map positions, grouped-channel equivalence or the Goldilocks target.
Replace every grouped position, point size and temporary rehearsal figure throughout the deck with documented results before the judged pitch.

motion.description: Reveal the three channel families with their unboxed paper conclusions, then reveal the Goldilocks combination on the fourth click.

slides.claim: 82% feel they do not fully show their appreciation; 71% say ordinary-day appreciation can feel awkward or out of place; the channel families each trade impact, friction and frequency.
slides.audience_takeaway: Read the survey story immediately as What, Why and How, without turning those labels back into three large questions.

visual.composition: Title the slide `Survey results` and restore small What / Why / How labels as an orientation layer, not three large questions. Treat 82% and its one-line meaning, then 71% and its one-line meaning, as two continuous headline blocks. Use a hand-drawn three-row trade-off ledger with one shared metric header, large channel icons and large values so it reads as one editorial field note rather than a miniature dashboard. On a fourth click, circle letter/gift impact, quick-text friction and voice/video frequency to show the three qualities the team wants to combine. A footer discloses that all values are temporary rehearsal figures rather than survey findings.

speaker_notes: Timing: 40 seconds.
Reveal the 82% and 71% findings directly, then reveal the three grouped form families and explain that each has strengths but no family captures all three.
Click once more to circle the three source qualities: letter/gift impact, text friction and voice/video frequency.
Every value is temporary rehearsal data. Replace it after recruitment, method, sample, wording, analysis, exact results, exceptions and limitations are recorded.
Psychology on text meaningfulness, synchronous voice/video and perceived effort supports only the channel mechanisms; it cannot validate these grouped figures or equivalence.

motion.description: Reveal the two headline findings and the compact channel ledger, then circle the three qualities the solution will combine.

slides.audience_takeaway: See the working market-gap need-state between a casual text and a high-friction letter or gift before meeting any individual example.

visual.composition: Use exactly three builds and two oversized cropped Goldilocks rings to divide the full 1600 by 900 canvas into three vertical bands. Build 1 reveals `text — too awkward or too casual`; build 2 reveals `letter / gift — too much; high friction; inaccessible`; build 3 adds a curved pale-blue band between the rings and lands only `Users are stuck in limbo.` Do not show a visible `MARKET GAP` label or add a supporting or explanatory sentence to the final reveal. Keep university students, long-distance family and close friends as working contexts in the footer, which must state that this is a working need-state hypothesis rather than validated market sizing or demand. Do not introduce Maya on this slide.

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Build 1 reveals the text-side constraint; build 2 reveals the letter-or-gift constraint; build 3 reveals the curved pale-blue market-gap band.
On the final build, land only: `Users are stuck in limbo.` Do not add a visible `MARKET GAP` label or a second explanatory sentence to the slide.
Keep university students, long-distance family and close friends as working contexts only. This is a need-state hypothesis, not validated market sizing, demand or prevalence.

motion.description: Use exactly three builds: reveal the text constraint, reveal the letter-or-gift constraint, then wash the curved pale-blue band into the middle and land only the single limbo headline.

slides.claim: Maya wants to thank someone for being so friendly during her first week at uni.
slides.audience_takeaway: See one concrete ordinary-Tuesday use case, while recognising that Maya and both percentages are illustrative rehearsal material rather than validated evidence.

visual.composition: Use a separate three-build illustrative-use-case slide. Begin exactly with `Maya wants to thank someone for being so friendly during her first week at uni.` Build 1 lands `It is an ordinary Tuesday.` Build 2 reveals the temporary rehearsal placeholder `72% said a text can feel too casual for meaningful appreciation.` Build 3 reveals the temporary placeholder `78% said they have never received a gift “just because.”` and closes with `Maya is one example of the people caught between both.` The footer must say that 72% and 78% are temporary rehearsal placeholders rather than verified primary-research findings and that Maya is illustrative, not a validated persona.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Introduce Maya with the exact scenario: `Maya wants to thank someone for being so friendly during her first week at uni.`

Build 1 establishes that it is an ordinary Tuesday. Build 2 reveals the 72% text-too-casual placeholder. Build 3 reveals the 78% never-received-a-just-because-gift placeholder, then closes that Maya is one example caught between both.

The 72% and 78% figures are temporary rehearsal placeholders, not verified primary findings. Maya is an illustrative scenario, not a validated persona, participant or segment. Do not present any of them as evidence.

motion.description: Use exactly three builds: ordinary Tuesday, the 72% text placeholder, then the 78% gift placeholder and the closing line that Maya is one example caught between both.

slides.claim: If the expression gap exists and ordinary-day appreciation feels awkward, then normalise the act by aiming for gift-level impact with digital-level friction and repeatability.
slides.audience_takeaway: Follow the evidence deduction into one explicit product requirement before the solution reveal.

visual.composition: Preserve the high-contrast If / And / Then chain. Add a fourth unboxed `Therefore` line at the bottom: create the impact of gift-giving with the low friction and repeatability of everyday digital contact. Use the same temporary 82% and 71% rehearsal figures as the survey-results slide, disclosed in the footer, until real results replace them.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
For rehearsal, connect the temporary What and Why figures, name normalising ordinary-day appreciation as the outcome, then state the product requirement in the Therefore line.
Replace the two temporary percentages before the judged pitch. The desired outcome and Goldilocks combination remain a design deduction, not a validated result.

motion.description: Reveal If, And, Then and the added Therefore requirement in order.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies is a personal digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the proposed solution, then why digital supports a broader authored form before the live demonstration.

visual.composition: Open with the existing large centred sentence exactly: `Warm & Fuzzies is a personal digital keepsake that brings the thoughtfulness of a letter to the ease of a text.` Emphasise the two borrowed qualities in the blue accent. On the second click, let the sentence recede beneath `Because digital can hold more than words.` and a spacious hand-drawn spectrum of writing, photo, voice, video and chosen-song icons. Do not add cards, a fake keepsake box, recipient copy, diamonds, a phone screenshot, product-name lockup, mechanism subtext or prototype footer.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.

Read or closely paraphrase the existing solution sentence. On the second click, say: `Because digital can hold more than words.` Name the expressive range—writing, photo, voice, video and a chosen song—then move into the product mechanics.

Treat thoughtfulness plus ease as the product proposition that the next slide and demo make legible, not as a validated superiority claim or measured outcome. The media range is an expressive capability, not proof of impact.

motion.description: Show the complete solution sentence, then reveal the digital-expression line and medium spectrum before handing off to the mechanics slide.

slides.claim: Warm & Fuzzies answers the format gap through four visible working-prototype mechanisms rather than an unsupported high-impact, low-friction score.
slides.audience_takeaway: See how each borrowed strength becomes a product mechanism and which part of the gap that mechanism is designed to answer before the live demo.

visual.composition: Use a three-column causal ledger headed `strength we borrow`, `working prototype mechanism` and `gap it answers`. Build 1 maps handwritten-letter personality to an authored canvas—words, layout and personal mark—then to `personal, not generic`. Build 2 maps mixed media to writing, photo, voice, video and song in one keepsake, then to `more than words`. Build 3 maps text to one direct browser link with no receiver account or download, then to `opens without setup`. Build 4 maps gift-like ownership to a receiver-controlled keepsake—keep, revisit or remove—then reveals a firefly-branded summary strip connecting implemented mechanisms to the design targets `impact`, `low friction` and `repeatability`. Use no product score, fake metric, Venn, screenshots or generic feature cards. Keep the footer explicit that outcomes are design targets, receiver control is not legal ownership and revisitability is not permanent storage.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Build 1: `We did not just borrow the idea of a letter; the working maker preserves your own words, layout and personal mark, so authorship stays visible.`
Build 2: `One keepsake can hold writing, photo, voice, video and a chosen song, so the form can fit the thought.`
Build 3: `It arrives through one direct browser link, with no receiver account or download, so opening does not introduce setup friction.`
Build 4: `The receiver decides whether to keep, revisit or remove the keepsake. Those mechanisms are how we are designing toward impact, low friction and repeatability.`

Do not call the link private: it can be forwarded. Receiver choice is not legal ownership, and revisitability is browser-local in the current prototype rather than permanent storage. The slide proves implemented mechanisms, not emotional impact, reduced awkwardness, market demand or superiority.

motion.description: Use exactly four builds. Each build reveals and highlights one complete source-to-mechanism-to-response row. On build four, retain the full ledger and reveal the firefly summary that maps mechanisms to the three Goldilocks design targets.

slides.audience_takeaway: Open the public demo by QR while watching one complete working sender-to-receiver journey rather than a narrated feature tour.

visual.composition: A dark live-demo handoff with `Follow along.` on the left and a large encoding-verified QR for `https://warm-and-fuzzies.vercel.app/demo/receive` on the right. Include the readable receiver URL and a no-phone instruction. No screenshots, process checklist or second closing slide.

speaker_notes: Timing: 100 seconds.
Invite the room to scan the replayable `/demo/receive` fixture if they want to follow on their own phone, then open `/demo/create` on the presentation screen.
Show only the critical path: name → make → seal → send → open → keep/remove.

Explain why each step exists while it appears: naming makes it personal; making makes authorship visible; sealing creates closure; sending lowers receiving friction; opening is on the receiver's terms; keep/remove gives the receiver the ending. Keep the emphasis on the research logic, not a separate process diary.
Close verbally: `The message can be complete when it arrives.`
Demonstrate only working states. Do not claim delivery infrastructure, verified identity, encrypted privacy, ownership, permanent storage or lower awkwardness.
The public QR is a fixed replayable receiver fixture, not a personalised thank-you, participant task or validation event.

motion.description: Show the QR once, then stop deck motion while the presenter demonstrates the working prototype.

appendix_contract.purpose: Give judges a fast, inspectable evidence and Q&A layer without adding to the 11-slide live pitch.
appendix_contract.winner_benchmark: Borrow the 2025 winner's separation between a sparse live story and a detailed research appendix, including raw-method visibility and references, without copying its visual identity.
appendix_contract.navigation: Deep links use ?slide=A1 through ?slide=A15; I opens the index; F toggles fullscreen; the single return control goes to live slide 11.
non_negotiable_boundaries: No completed primary study currently validates the expression gap, occasion rule, market, audience, product outcome or superiority.
The 82%, 71%, 72%, 78%, 1–5 ratings, chart positions and dot sizes are quarantined rehearsal placeholders.
Published studies support adjacent mechanisms only; no study directly validates Warm & Fuzzies.
Prototype screenshots and the live flow prove implemented behaviour only, not desirability or social change.
Unknown team metadata, consent and 2026 disclosure requirements remain visibly incomplete rather than invented.
